title: Non-blocking test-quality findings from frontend-daily-homework-history-followups' PR review (#403)
description: pr-reviewer's full review of PR #403 (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups, which extended the e2e suite and a component test, and recorded a decisions entry) accepted it -- tests/coverage, static analysis, make e2e (run twice, plus once with a deliberately reintroduced regression to confirm the new e2e assertions are load-bearing), and the dev-DB/decisions-append checks all passed. A `code-review` skill pass dispatched alongside that review surfaced two non-blocking test-quality findings in the new e2e assertions this PR added, which shouldn't disappear once PR #403 merges.

checklist.step: `frontend/tests/e2e/daily-homework.spec.ts`'s new History-row date assertion (around line 100) computes 'today' client-side via `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)` *after* the Save click, form re-render, and banner assertions have already elapsed, while the backend stamps the row's date via `today()` (backend/app/time_utils.py) at POST-handling time, earlier in that same sequence. A suite run straddling a UTC-midnight boundary between those two moments would see the stored and asserted dates disagree -- a narrow, low-probability latent flake this diff newly introduced (the spec made no date-sensitive assertions before this PR). Fix by reading the date back from the POST response (or the rendered form/banner) instead of recomputing 'today' independently client-side, so the assertion can never disagree with what the backend actually stored.

`expectedHistoryDateCell` (frontend/tests/e2e/daily-homework.spec.ts line 35) re-implements `formatDate`'s (frontend/src/utils/format.ts) exact `toLocaleDateString` options inline instead of importing `formatDate` directly (available -- `tsconfig.app.json` includes both `src` and `tests`), or adding a shared helper under `tests/` the way `tests/dateFixtures.ts`'s `isoDateWeeksAgo` already does for an analogous need shared between MSW mocks and e2e specs. If `formatDate`'s options ever change, this copy won't follow, and the e2e assertion would start failing for a reason unrelated to any real regression. Replace the local re-implementation with a direct import of `formatDate`.

comments.summary: Verified `page.waitForResponse` is registered before the triggering Save click (via `Promise.all`, not after), so it genuinely eliminates the UTC-midnight race rather than relocating it -- confirmed by reading the diff directly, not just the PR description.

Confirmed the History-row date assertion is still load-bearing after the change: mutated DailyHomeworkHistoryTable.tsx's date-cell render to append a stray character, re-ran the spec, and it failed with the expected text mismatch; reverted and re-ran make e2e clean (28/28).

Confirmed the spec now imports and uses the real `formatDate` (frontend/src/utils/format.ts) rather than a local copy, with matching `toLocaleDateString` options to what was removed. This is the first e2e spec under frontend/tests/e2e/ to import anything from `src/` directly (every other spec's shared helper, e.g. `isoDateWeeksAgo`, comes from tests/dateFixtures.ts instead) -- correct for this specific fix (the parent task's checklist explicitly called for a direct import), but a new precedent worth an explicit convention decision for future specs. Non-blocking; tracked as a follow-up task.

review.notes: make e2e: 28/28 passed (confirmed independently, not just the claimed figure). Backend pytest --cov=app: 1618 passed, 99.94% coverage. Frontend vitest --coverage: 1054 passed across 101 files, 99.78%/99.05%/99.84%/99.81% (statements/branches/functions/lines) -- both well above the 90% gate, no regression. Backend+frontend ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc and scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py and scripts/validate_tasks.py all clean. The code-review skill (medium effort) found no concrete bugs. No application code is touched by this PR (only the e2e spec plus task-board JSON), so no OpenAPI/API-doc check applies and no browser (Playwright MCP) walkthrough was run -- there's no new UI behavior for one to exercise; the persisted e2e suite (make e2e) is the directly relevant check here and was run as above. One non-blocking finding (the new src/-import precedent) filed as a followup task per CLAUDE.md's non-blocking-finding tracking rule.

decisions.decision: Fixed the UTC-midnight date race by capturing the POST /api/daily-homework response itself (via `page.waitForResponse` wrapped around the Save click) and reading its `date` field back as `recordedDate`, rather than accepting either adjacent calendar date or restructuring the assertion order so the client-side 'today' computation happens closer to the POST. `recordedDate` is then passed through the real `formatDate` helper (imported directly, closing the second finding too) for the History-row cell assertion.
decisions.rationale: This is the only option of the three considered that makes the assertion compare against the literal value the backend actually persisted, so it can never disagree with it regardless of timing -- not just less likely to disagree. Accepting either of two adjacent dates would still pass on a wrong-looking assertion (weakening what's actually being verified, which the e2e-test skill's 'don't weaken a spec to make it pass' rule and this task's own description discourage) and wouldn't catch a genuine backend date-stamping bug as precisely. Reordering the assertions so the client-side 'today' snapshot is taken immediately after the Save click (before the banner/form-rerender assertions) would narrow the race window but not eliminate it -- there's always some nonzero gap between the click resolving and `new Date()` evaluating, and the backend's own clock read happens strictly earlier in the request lifecycle than either. Reading the POST response's own `date` field removes the client-side 'today' guess entirely, which is also a smaller diff than reordering every assertion in the test body. `DailyHomeworkOut.date` is already a stable, documented field on the exact response type `recordDailyHomework` (frontend/src/api/homework.ts) returns, so no backend or schema change was needed.
